details.publicNotes:
In realms overtaken by shadows, animals made of solidified darkness roam, taking multitudes of shapes and sizes. The species of these unusual creatures most often encountered outside their domain are oversized rodents which are known as giant gloom rats, though they wander into the light mainly due to necessity. They resemble the pure black silhouettes of giant rats, except that they have one large eye that glows brightly in the murk.

People often assume that creatures made of darkness would hate the light, but giant gloom rats actually swarm around the rare source of light in their homes, eating it as fast as they can. Because of this particular diet, giant gloom rats proliferate wildly when they manage to break into other places full of natural light.

This rapid reproduction can cause mayhem when nobles and rich merchants take giant gloom rats as pets to show off their wealth. Giant gloom rats seem to enjoy these arrangements for a while, so long as they are well-fed and provided with regular entertainment. When they get bored, however, they often sneak away into the streets and start eating all of the light sources in their surroundings. Not all gloom rat infestations are accidents; thieves, assassins, and others who benefit from a sudden loss of visibility at night sometimes unleash the rats to darken the streets.

Gloom Fever

Scholars researching gloom fever often speculate on the nature of the disease. After all, in the shadowy realms from which gloom rats originate, light sources are few and far between. Prevailing theories include the idea that the disease represents an infusion of elemental shadow or that it is carried by microscopic pathogens native to shadowy realms that flourish within gloom rats' bodies. Some even theorize that the disease evolved to encourage infected people to keep gloom rats as pets, as they would come to rely on the rats to extinguish troublesome light sources. Regardless of its origin, people don't always view the disease as a threat. People who expect to be without light for long periods of time have been known to deliberately infect themselves with the disease.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 7/18/30 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning, piercing), armor (light), perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, constitution, darkness, dexterity, energy resistant (vitality), sensory (darkvision, greater darkvision), wild

description.value: A giant gloom rat's eye can pierce most shadows. When its eye is opened, it can't be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC] by darkness, unless the effect can also block darkvision. When its eye is closed, it is naturally invisible in dim light and darkness, as its body blends with surrounding shadows.

Requirements The giant gloom rat's last action was a successful jaws Strike against a creature or unattended object, and that creature or object is emanating light

Effect The giant gloom rat attempts to counteract one source of light on the target, or an object it is holding or wearing, with a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+9 #Counteract]]{+9}. If the source of light is mundane, the light is automatically snuffed out. If the source is magical and the counteract check is successful, the giant gloom rat gains temporary Hit Points equal to double the counteract rank of the effect (minimum 2).

A creature afflicted with this disease takes a –2 status penalty to all visual Perception checks

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:17]

Stage 1 carrier with only the base effect (1d4 hours)

Stage 2 light blindness (1 day)

Stage 3 light blindness and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} when in dim light (1 day)

Stage 4 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} when in bright light and dazzled when in dim light, gains low-light vision (1 day)

Stage 5 blinded when in bright or dim light, gains darkvision (1 day)
